        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 95093595914c17f32e1d6228b4db06fab8cebd35 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Lv Ruyi <lv.ruyi@zte.com.cn>
Date: Mon, 25 Apr 2022 09:09:47 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] drm/msm/dpu: fix error check return value of
 irq_of_parse_and_map()

The irq_of_parse_and_map() function returns 0 on failure, and does not
return a negative value anyhow, so never enter this conditional branch.

Fixes: 25fdd5933e4c ("drm/msm: Add SDM845 DPU support")
Reported-by: Zeal Robot <zealci@zte.com.cn>
Signed-off-by: Lv Ruyi <lv.ruyi@zte.com.cn>
Reviewed-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org>
Patchwork: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/483291/
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220425090947.3498897-1-lv.ruyi@zte.com.cn
Signed-off-by: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@linaro.org>
---
 drivers/gpu/drm/msm/disp/dpu1/dpu_kms.c | 6 +++---
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/disp/dpu1/dpu_kms.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/disp/dpu1/dpu_kms.c
index c683cab0dc31..3316b964d4f3 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/disp/dpu1/dpu_kms.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/disp/dpu1/dpu_kms.c
@@ -1183,9 +1183,9 @@ static int dpu_kms_init(struct drm_device *ddev)
 	priv->kms = &dpu_kms->base;
 
 	irq = irq_of_parse_and_map(dpu_kms->pdev->dev.of_node, 0);
-	if (irq < 0) {
-		DPU_ERROR("failed to get irq: %d\n", irq);
-		return irq;
+	if (!irq) {
+		DPU_ERROR("failed to get irq\n");
+		return -EINVAL;
 	}
 	dpu_kms->base.irq = irq;
 
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by an incorrect error check for the return value of the `irq_of_parse_and_map()` function. The original code incorrectly assumed that the function could return a negative value to indicate an error, but in reality, it returns 0 on failure. This led to the conditional branch being entered incorrectly, which would not handle the error case properly. The patch corrects this by checking for a return value of 0 instead, ensuring that the error handling logic is executed correctly when the function fails.

The original code incorrectly assumed that the function could return a negative value to indicate an error, but in reality, it returns 0 on failure. This led to the conditional branch being entered incorrectly, which would not handle the error case properly. The patch corrects this by checking for a return value of 0 instead, ensuring that the error handling logic is executed correctly when the function fails.
